headline: Friday slate: Nations League (France-Italy, Belgium-Türkiye), Friday night college football, a 5-game NHL card, WNBA Wings-Valkyries Game 3, and Round 2 at the Bank of Utah. No MLB today — the Division Series start Saturday.

record.label: Yesterday (Thu 10/1)
record.note: Props went 6-2 and the Braves SGP hit; all three game totals lost. Golf picks settle Sunday.

notes: No bet is a lock. 'Confidence' runs 1–5, and nothing on this board is above a 4.
Nations League matches kick off at 11:45 AM PT — bet those first or skip them.
Odds move. Skip any pick whose price is past the 'playable to' number in its reasoning.
Same-game parlay (SGP) prices are set by the book and pay less than the multiplied odds shown here.

sections.label: Best of the Day
sections.slate: The strongest edges across today's card. Thursday these went 4-3-1 (+0.57u); the props carried it.

straight.reasoning: This is the biggest goalie mismatch on the board. The Jets suspended Connor Hellebuyck for not reporting to camp while he pushes for a trade, so Stuart Skinner starts. Boston has Jeremy Swayman. Boston has won its last two meetings with Winnipeg, and both SI and SportsBettingDime have the Bruins as a best bet. A coin-flip price with a real goaltending edge is the value. Playable to -115.

+1.25 means Türkiye wins the bet with a win or draw, gets half back on a 1-goal loss, and loses only on a 2+ goal loss. Belgium has failed to cover -1.25 in 13 of its last 20 home games, and Türkiye has covered +1.25 in 17 of its last 20 away games. Belgium also looked toothless in its last match: two shots on target in a 1-0 home loss to France. Playable to -135.

These teams have cleared this number in four of their five meetings this season. Game 2 went to overtime behind Arike Ogunbowale's 45 points. Dimers' model rates the Over at 159.5 as its second-best play of the day, so 157.5 is two points of extra cushion. Thursday's Over lost by 3.5, so this is one unit, not a max bet. Playable to 159.5.

parlay.title: Friday Three-Sport
parlay.reasoning: Three independent legs across three sports. Golden State is 17-5 at home and won all three regular-season meetings by 8+, and Dallas is missing Azzi Fudd and Alanna Smith. Adding the big Valkyries favorite boosts the payout without adding much risk.

parlay.title: Safer Two-Legger
parlay.reasoning: Two home favorites with clear edges. Dallas has won 13 of its last 20 home games and plays its home opener against a low-event Blues team. Golden State has the league's top defense at home. Together they pay roughly even money.

props.reasoning: Dimers projects 11.2 rebounds, a 66% hit rate against an implied 59%. Dallas is missing two bigs (Alanna Smith out, Awak Kuier only probable), which opens up the glass. Playable to -160.

The Rangers start backup Dylan Garand instead of Igor Shesterkin. Garand had a .896 save percentage in the AHL last season. New York has given up 7.43 expected goals in two games. Raymond is Detroit's top winger, and with Dylan Larkin out he gets even more of the offense. Covers gives him a 62% chance. Playable to -170.
Güler has a shot on target in three straight games and takes Türkiye's set pieces and long-range shots. One on target clears this. Confirm he's in the lineup (posted about an hour before kickoff).

sections.label: Baseball
sections.slate: Off day. The Division Series start Saturday: White Sox @ Guardians, Braves @ Dodgers, Yankees @ Rays, Padres @ Brewers. Saturday's board will have them.

sections.label: Football
sections.slate: No NFL tonight. Friday night college football: Penn State @ Northwestern, Pitt @ Virginia Tech (both 4-0), Idaho @ Montana State, Liberty vs Delaware.

straight.reasoning: This is Dimers' top college play of the day: a 53.5% cover rate at almost even money. Penn State's passing game stalled against Wisconsin, with a 23% success rate on 31 attempts, and they blew a 17-7 halftime lead. Aidan Chiles has a 56% success rate against the Cover 3 and Cover 1 looks Penn State plays most. Take +3 if you can find it.

Both teams are 4-0, both lean on their defenses, and Pitt's games have gone Under three times in four. In an unbeaten-vs-unbeaten ACC game, expect conservative play-calling and a field-position fight. This is a lean, not a strong play.

Dimers' model gives Idaho a 55.5% chance to cover, its second-best college edge of the day. In a conference rivalry, two touchdowns is a lot of points. Half unit, since FCS lines carry less information.

parlay.title: Friday Night Dogs
parlay.reasoning: The two underdogs Dimers' model rates highest. Together they pay about 2.7-to-1.

sections.label: Soccer
sections.slate: UEFA Nations League at 11:45 AM PT: France vs Italy, Belgium vs Türkiye, Bosnia vs Sweden, Poland vs Romania. These start soon — bet them first.

straight.reasoning: Belgium has failed to cover -1.25 in 13 of its last 20 home games, and Türkiye has covered +1.25 in 17 of its last 20 away games. Belgium managed two shots on target in its last match, a 1-0 home loss to France. A draw or Türkiye win pays in full, and a 1-goal Belgium win returns half your stake. Playable to -135.

France is at home at the Stade de France and has two straight 1-0 wins under Zinedine Zidane. Italy is without left back Federico Dimarco. France is missing Mbappé, Saliba and Tchouaméni, which is why this is 0.75u and not more. Playable to -165.
Sweden has five goals in two Nations League games but hasn't kept a clean sheet. A side that scores freely and concedes freely is the standard setup for an Over. Half unit.

parlay.title: Nations League Double
parlay.reasoning: Both legs settle at the same time. Note: on a 1-goal Belgium win the Türkiye leg is a half-loss, and most books grade that leg as a loss in a parlay.

props.reasoning: Güler has a shot on target in three straight games and takes Türkiye's set pieces and long shots. Confirm he starts before betting.

sections.label: Hockey
sections.slate: Five games: Rangers @ Red Wings, Capitals @ Hurricanes, Bruins @ Jets, Blues @ Stars (Dallas home opener), Ducks @ Golden Knights.

straight.reasoning: Winnipeg suspended Connor Hellebuyck for not reporting to camp, so Stuart Skinner starts against Jeremy Swayman. Boston has won its last two meetings with Winnipeg. SI and SportsBettingDime both have the Bruins. Playable to -115.

Shesterkin carried the Rangers on Thursday — 24 saves plus an empty-net goal — and he sits tonight on the back end of a back-to-back. Backup Dylan Garand had a .896 save percentage in the AHL. New York has given up 7.43 expected goals in two games. Playable to -150.

Brandon Bussi stonewalled Florida on opening night in a 1-0 OT loss, and Logan Thompson is one of the steadiest goalies in the league. Both teams play structured defense. It takes 7 goals to lose this bet.

parlay.title: Backup Goalie Fade
parlay.reasoning: Same idea in both games: bet against the team starting a backup goalie. Winnipeg is without Hellebuyck and the Rangers are without Shesterkin. Pays about 3-to-1.

parlay.title: Stars Home Opener (SGP)
parlay.reasoning: Covers' combo for this game. If Johnston scores, Rantanen is likely to have assisted on it, and Dallas is likely to win. Johnston scored in 50% of his home games last season. Prop odds are estimates; check your book.

props.reasoning: Detroit's top winger faces backup Dylan Garand (.896 AHL save percentage) behind a defense allowing 7.43 expected goals through two games. With Dylan Larkin out, Raymond's role grows. Covers puts it at 62%. Playable to -170.

Rantanen had an assist in 66% of games last season, 70% at home, and 73% when Dallas was a -150 or bigger favorite. He plays with finishers Wyatt Johnston and Jason Robertson, against a St. Louis penalty kill that was ninth-worst last year. Playable to -140.

DeBrincat scored in 55% of Detroit's home games as a favorite last season, and tonight he faces the Rangers' backup goalie. Covers rates it at 43%; at +135 (about 42.5% implied) the value is thin, so it's a quarter unit.

sections.label: Golf
sections.slate: Bank of Utah Championship, Round 2 (in progress — prices are live). Zach Bauchou leads at -9 after a 62; nine players are at -8; defending champ Michael Brennan is -7. The field averaged about 68 on Thursday. Yesterday's golf picks (Ben James T10, Brennan T20, Keefer T20) are still live.

straight.reasoning: The defending champion opened with a 64 and is two shots back. After Round 1 he ranked 2nd in strokes gained off the tee and 5th in approach, so his ball striking is producing the score, not his putting. On a course that has needed -22 or better to win, he's on pace. The price is an estimate; it moves with every hole.

props.pick: Michael Brennan to lead after Round 2
props.reasoning: He won here last year after moving into a share of the lead on Friday. Lineups.com flags +1300 as value given his course history and that he's two back. A long shot, so a quarter unit.
Keefer's ball-striking numbers are better than Hall's, and Keefer was near the top of the board through much of Round 1. Matchups remove the rest of the field from the equation. Price is an estimate.

sections.label: Basketball
sections.slate: WNBA Playoffs Game 3, winner-take-all: Wings @ Valkyries (series 1-1). NBA preseason starts Saturday.

straight.reasoning: These teams have cleared this number in four of five meetings this season, and Game 2 went to overtime behind Ogunbowale's 45 points. Dimers rates the Over at 159.5 as a top play, and the current 157.5 gives two more points of cushion. Playable to 159.5.

parlay.title: Valkyries Control the Glass (SGP)
parlay.reasoning: Golden State is 17-5 at home and Dallas is missing two bigs. If Shepard dominates the boards, the Valkyries probably win. The expensive moneyline is better used as a parlay leg than bet alone.

props.reasoning: Dimers projects 11.2 rebounds (a 66% hit rate). Dallas's frontcourt is thin, with Alanna Smith out and Awak Kuier only probable. Playable to -160.
Dimers projects 13.3 points for Williams — six under the line — the biggest edge (11%) on its board. A line this far above her projection suggests it was set off one big game.

She shot 32.5% from three this season and made 2+ threes in only 20 games. After her 45-point Game 2, this line is inflated by recency, and Golden State has the league's best defense. Plus money for a likely outcome.
